_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Based on the AssaultCube egg in https://github.com/pterodactyl/game-eggs (MIT).
name: AssaultCube
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: AssaultCube, the free fast-paced multiplayer shooter. It uses the server port and the next one up, and is listed on the master server once it has a server key.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# AssaultCube: downloads a release from GitHub and keeps what the server
# needs (the server, its config folder and the official maps). Config files
# are added only when they aren't there yet, so your edits are kept.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server

repo=assaultcube/AC
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }
build=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
trap 'rm -rf "$build"' EXIT

want="${VERSION:-latest}"
if [ "$want" = latest ]; then
    tag=$(gh-release tag "$repo") || fail "GitHub can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."
else
    case "$want" in v*) ;; *) want="v$want" ;; esac
    tag=$(gh-release tag "$repo" "$want" 2>/dev/null) ||
        fail "AssaultCube has no version $want. Set Version to latest, or to a release such as $(gh-release tag "$repo" 2>/dev/null || echo v1.3.0.2)."
fi
asset=$(gh-release assets "$repo" "$tag" | awk '{print $1}' | grep -E '\.tar\.bz2$' | head -n1 || true)
[ -n "$asset" ] || fail "AssaultCube $tag has no Linux download."

if [ -x bin_unix/linux_64_server ] && [ "$(cat .raptor-version 2>/dev/null)" = "$tag" ]; then
    echo "AssaultCube $tag is already installed."
else
    mkdir -p "$build/x"
    echo "Downloading AssaultCube $tag"
    gh-release download "$repo" "$tag" "$asset" "$build/ac.tar.bz2" || fail "The download failed. Reinstall to try again."
    tar -xjf "$build/ac.tar.bz2" -C "$build/x" --wildcards './bin_unix/linux_64_server' './config/*' './packages/maps/*' ||
        fail "AssaultCube $tag has no Linux server in its download."
    rm -f "$build/ac.tar.bz2"
    # Config files are the server's own once they're there.
    (cd "$build/x" && find config -type f) | while read -r f; do
        if [ -e "$f" ]; then rm -f "$build/x/$f"; fi
    done
    cp -a "$build/x/." .
    chmod +x bin_unix/linux_64_server
    echo "$tag" > .raptor-version
fi

# The example command line file has a well-known server key; the key is
# the Server key variable instead.
if [ -f config/servercmdline.txt ]; then
    sed -i '/^-Y AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA/d' config/servercmdline.txt
fi
mkdir -p demos logs
echo "Installed AssaultCube $tag."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The AssaultCube release, such as v1.3.0.2, or latest for the newest one. Reinstall the server after changing it.

variables.name: Server key
variables.description: Your private server key (64 hex characters, made in the game with authkey new server). Without one the server is LAN only.

variables.name: Description
variables.description: The server's name in the server browser.

variables.name: Message of the day
variables.description: The message players see when they join.

variables.name: Max players
variables.description: The most players that can be on the server.

variables.name: Admin password
variables.description: The password to claim admin on the server. Leave it empty for none.

variables.name: Player password
variables.description: The password players need to join. Leave it empty for a public server.

variables.name: Master server
variables.description: The master server the server registers with.
